page: Microsoft Azure D16ds_v6 is a general-purpose virtual machine belonging to the Ddsv6 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and INT8 operations. The system is equipped with 64.0 GB of RAM, providing 4.0 GB of memory per core, and includes a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD.

Benchmark results place the D16ds_v6 in the average performance tier for most standard operations. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is measured at 1708.19, while the multi-core score reaches 13304.69. Memory bandwidth tests show a read-only small block cached speed of 1035.16 GB/sec, which drops to 105.59 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and a write speed of 54.61 GB/sec. In database operations, the instance achieves a PassMark database score of 7714.45 and processes 19.51 million Redis SET operations per second.

For machine learning workloads, the server demonstrates strong text generation performance with a small 135M parameter LLM, reaching 292.48 tokens/sec, though prompt processing for the same model averages 1464.17 tokens/sec. Larger models show typical CPU-bound constraints, with a 7B model achieving 14.67 tokens/sec for text generation and a 70B model processing prompts at 9.65 tokens/sec. From a resource-density perspective, the inclusion of a 945 GB NVMe SSD provides cost-efficient local storage capacity, making the instance suitable for workloads requiring fast temporary storage, such as software compilation (Clang benchmark score of 15256.0) and static web serving (throughput of 24.09 GB/sec).

Operating at 4.2 GHz, the CPU features a 260 MB L3 cache and supports Intel AMX and AVX-512 instructions. The instance includes a bundled 945 GB local NVMe SSD, providing fast temporary storage. Benchmark data indicates average performance across standard compute and memory tasks, with a PassMark CPU score of 22224.0 and a Redis SET throughput of 19.51 million operations per second. This hardware profile is suited for general-purpose workloads, software compilation, database operations, and web serving.
